question: According to the manual, why might steering away from an obstacle be a better response than trying to stop?
choice_a: Because you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Because steering causes less tire wear than braking
choice_c: Because most states require drivers to avoid braking in traffic
choice_d: Because steering keeps the cargo from shifting
explanation: The manual states you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop, which is why stopping is not always the safest response in an emergency.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: The manual warns that which types of vehicles may flip over when a driver makes a quick steering maneuver to avoid a crash?
choice_a: Vehicles equipped with antilock brakes
choice_b: Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers
choice_c: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials placards
choice_d: Empty straight trucks
explanation: The manual notes that although you can almost always turn faster than you can stop, top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over during a quick turn.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: To be able to turn quickly in an emergency, what does the manual advise drivers to do?
choice_a: Keep one hand on the wheel and one on the gearshift at all times
choice_b: Rest a hand near the horn while driving
choice_c: Keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times
choice_d: Loosen their grip on the wheel to react faster
explanation: The manual says the best way to have both hands on the wheel if an emergency occurs is to keep them there all the time, since a firm two-handed grip is needed to turn quickly.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: When returning to the road after being forced onto the shoulder, what does the manual say a driver should avoid?
choice_a: Using the turn signal
choice_b: Edging gradually back onto the road
choice_c: Braking before returning to the pavement
choice_d: Checking the mirrors
explanation: The manual warns not to edge gradually back onto the road, because the tires might grab unexpectedly and cause a loss of control; instead, turn sharply enough to get back on safely.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.1, Returning to the Road

question: When both front tires are back on the paved surface after leaving the road, what does the manual say the driver should do?
choice_a: Brake firmly before continuing
choice_b: Counter-steer immediately in a single "steer-counter-steer" move
choice_c: Come to a complete stop first
choice_d: Turn off the emergency flashers
explanation: The manual instructs that once both front tires are on the paved surface, the driver should counter-steer immediately, making the two turns as a single steer-counter-steer move.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.1, Returning to the Road

question: If a driver must leave the road in an emergency, what does the manual recommend about braking?
choice_a: Brake as hard as possible immediately
choice_b: Never use the brakes while off the road
choice_c: Avoid using the brakes until speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake very gently
choice_d: Pump the brakes continuously at highway speed
explanation: The manual's guidelines for leaving the road say to avoid braking until speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.1, Leaving the Road

question: In the "controlled braking" method described in the manual, what should a driver do if the wheels lock up while braking hard?
choice_a: Continue pressing the brake pedal harder
choice_b: Shift into a higher gear
choice_c: Release the brakes, then re-apply them as soon as possible
choice_d: Turn the steering wheel sharply
explanation: With controlled braking, if the wheels lock, the manual says to release the brakes and re-apply them as soon as you can, while keeping steering movements small.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely (Controlled Braking)

question: With the "stab braking" method, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again after the brakes are released?
choice_a: Up to one second
choice_b: About five seconds
choice_c: Up to ten seconds
choice_d: Wheels start rolling instantly
explanation: The manual states it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling again after the brakes are released during stab braking.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely (Stab Braking)

question: What happens, according to the manual, if a driver re-applies the brakes with the stab braking method before the wheels start rolling again?
choice_a: The vehicle stops faster
choice_b: The vehicle won't straighten out
choice_c: The ABS activates automatically
choice_d: Nothing different happens
explanation: The manual warns that if you re-apply the brakes before the wheels start rolling again, the vehicle won't straighten out.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely (Stab Braking)

question: According to the manual, what is wrong with "jamming on the brakes" during an emergency stop?
choice_a: It engages the parking brake unintentionally
choice_b: It overheats the ABS sensors
choice_c: It is illegal in commercial vehicles
choice_d: It keeps the wheels locked up and causes a skid, making the vehicle uncontrollable
explanation: The manual says emergency braking does not mean jamming the pedal down as hard as possible, because that keeps the wheels locked and causes a skid, and a skidding vehicle cannot be controlled.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.2, Don't Jam on the Brakes

question: According to the manual, most hydraulic brake failures occur for one of two reasons. What are they?
choice_a: Worn tires and bad alignment
choice_b: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
choice_c: Engine overheating and low fuel
choice_d: Faulty ABS sensors and a dead battery
explanation: The manual states most hydraulic brake failures occur for one of two reasons: loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade on long hills.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.3, Brake Failure

question: When a hydraulic brake system loses pressure, how does the brake pedal typically feel?
choice_a: Unusually stiff and hard to press
choice_b: It vibrates rapidly
choice_c: Spongy or it goes to the floor
choice_d: It locks in place
explanation: The manual explains that when the system won't build up pressure, the brake pedal will feel spongy or go to the floor.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.3, Loss of Hydraulic Pressure

question: Besides downshifting and pumping the brakes, what other method does the manual describe for slowing a vehicle after hydraulic brake failure, noting it is separate from the hydraulic system?
choice_a: The trailer hand valve
choice_b: Using the parking (emergency) brake
choice_c: Shutting off the fuel supply
choice_d: Turning off the engine
explanation: The manual notes the parking or emergency brake is separate from the hydraulic brake system, so it can be used to slow the vehicle when hydraulic brakes fail.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.3, Brake Failure

question: When using the parking brake to slow a vehicle after hydraulic brake failure, what must the driver do at the same time, according to the manual?
choice_a: Shift into neutral
choice_b: Turn on the hazard lights
choice_c: Press the release button or pull the release lever to adjust brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up
choice_d: Sound the horn continuously
explanation: The manual says to press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time you use the emergency brake, so you can adjust brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.3, Use the Parking Brake

question: If a truck's brakes fail on a long downgrade, what does the manual say is the driver's "best hope"?
choice_a: Shifting into neutral and coasting to a stop
choice_b: An escape ramp
choice_c: Pulling only the trailer's emergency brake
choice_d: Turning on the four-way flashers and waiting
explanation: The manual states that once brakes have failed on a downgrade, your best hope is an escape ramp, and if one is available, signs will tell you about it.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.3, Brake Failure on Downgrades

question: According to the manual, what is an easily recognized sign of a tire blowout?
choice_a: A loud "bang"
choice_b: A burning smell
choice_c: The steering wheel becoming loose
choice_d: A dashboard warning light turning red
explanation: The manual describes the loud "bang" of a blowout as an easily recognized sign, and says any time you hear a tire blow, assume it's yours.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.4, Recognize Tire Failure

question: If a rear tire fails, what does the manual say usually prevents the vehicle from "fishtailing"?
choice_a: The trailer brakes
choice_b: Dual rear tires
choice_c: The ABS system
choice_d: A fully loaded cargo bed
explanation: The manual states that failure of a rear tire will sometimes cause the vehicle to slide back and forth or "fishtail," but dual rear tires usually prevent this.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.4, Recognize Tire Failure

question: When a tire fails, what does the manual instruct a driver to do regarding the brakes?
choice_a: Brake hard immediately to stop as fast as possible
choice_b: Apply only the parking brake
choice_c: Stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake gently
choice_d: Pump the brakes rapidly
explanation: The manual says that unless you're about to run into something, you should stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake very gently, pull off the road, and stop.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.4, Respond to Tire Failure

question: After a tire failure and coming to a stop, what does the manual say a driver should do, even if the vehicle seemed to be handling all right?
choice_a: Immediately call for roadside assistance
choice_b: Get out and check all the tires
choice_c: Continue driving to the next exit
choice_d: Release the parking brake
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to get out and check all the tires after stopping, even if the vehicle seemed fine, because if a dual tire fails the only way you may know is by looking at it.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.17.4, Respond to Tire Failure

question: What does ABS do to a vehicle's normal braking capability?
choice_a: It increases stopping power on wet roads
choice_b: It does not decrease or increase normal braking capability
choice_c: It decreases braking capability slightly for safety
choice_d: It replaces the normal hydraulic brake system
explanation: The manual states ABS is an addition to your normal brakes and does not decrease or increase your normal braking capability; it only activates when wheels are about to lock up.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: What does an ABS electronic control unit (ECU) do when sensors detect potential wheel lockup?
choice_a: It increases brake pressure to stop faster
choice_b: It disengages the transmission
choice_c: It sounds an audible alarm only
choice_d: It decreases brake pressure to avoid wheel lockup
explanation: The manual explains that sensors detect potential wheel lockup, and the ECU will then decrease brake pressure to avoid wheel lockup.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.1, How Antilock Braking Systems Work

question: Per the manual, ABS is required on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_b: January 1, 1995
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: July 1, 2000
explanation: The manual states the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.2, Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,000 lbs or more are required to have ABS if built on or after:
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: March 1, 2001
explanation: The manual states hydraulically braked trucks and buses with a GVWR of 10,000 lbs or more built on or after March 1, 1999 are required to have ABS.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.2, Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: On trailers, where does the manual say the yellow ABS malfunction lamp is located?
choice_a: On the left side, either the front or rear corner
choice_b: On the instrument panel
choice_c: On the rear bumper only
choice_d: Inside the cab dashboard
explanation: The manual says trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.3, How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: According to the manual, what happens if a vehicle's steering wheels lock up during hard braking without ABS?
choice_a: The vehicle automatically shifts to a lower gear
choice_b: The driver loses steering control
choice_c: The parking brake engages automatically
choice_d: The trailer detaches
explanation: The manual explains that when your steering wheels lock up, you lose steering control, and when other wheels lock up you may skid, jackknife, or spin the vehicle.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.4, How ABS Helps You

question: What is the one exception the manual describes to braking normally on a vehicle equipped with ABS?
choice_a: On wet roads, drivers should pump the brakes instead
choice_b: On downgrades, ABS should be turned off
choice_c: When towing, only the trailer brakes should be used
choice_d: In an emergency stop, a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles can fully apply the brakes
explanation: The manual states there is only one exception to braking as you always have: if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.6, Braking with ABS

question: The manual states that ABS will NOT do which of the following?
choice_a: Compensate for bad brakes or poor brake maintenance
choice_b: Help maintain vehicle control during hard braking
choice_c: Work as an addition to normal brakes
choice_d: Warn the driver of a malfunction with a lamp
explanation: Among the safety reminders, the manual states ABS won't compensate for bad brakes or poor brake maintenance.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.18.8, Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual, what are the four causes of skids?
choice_a: Over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast
choice_b: Bald tires, rain, ice, and fog
choice_c: Overloading, poor alignment, worn brakes, and low tire pressure
choice_d: Speeding, tailgating, distracted driving, and fatigue
explanation: The manual lists four causes of skids: over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast for conditions.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.19, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What does the manual describe as "by far the most common skid"?
choice_a: A front-wheel skid caused by worn tread
choice_b: A skid where the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
choice_c: A skid caused by crosswinds
choice_d: A skid caused by an ABS malfunction
explanation: The manual states that by far the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.19.1, Drive-wheel Skids

question: In a vehicle towing a trailer, what can a drive-wheel skid cause, according to the manual?
choice_a: The trailer to push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife
choice_b: The trailer brakes to lock automatically
choice_c: The tractor to accelerate uncontrollably
choice_d: The ABS malfunction lamp to activate
explanation: The manual explains that with vehicles towing trailers, a drive-wheel skid can let the trailer push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.19.1, Drive-wheel Skids

question: What is the first step the manual gives for correcting a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake
choice_b: Downshift immediately
choice_c: Stop braking, to let the rear wheels roll again
choice_d: Turn on the hazard lights
explanation: The manual's first step for correcting a drive-wheel braking skid is to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.19.2, Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: The manual recommends practicing skid-recovery skills like counter-steering in which location?
choice_a: An empty interstate highway
choice_b: A parking garage
choice_c: A commercial truck weigh station
choice_d: A large driving range or "skid pad"
explanation: The manual states the best place to practice staying off the brake, turning quickly, and counter-steering in a skid is on a large driving range or "skid pad."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.19.2, Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: In a front-wheel skid, how does the vehicle typically behave regardless of how much the steering wheel is turned?
choice_a: It spins in a complete circle
choice_b: The front end tends to go in a straight line
choice_c: It automatically corrects itself
choice_d: It rolls onto its side
explanation: The manual explains that in a front-wheel skid, the front end tends to go in a straight line regardless of how much the driver turns the steering wheel.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.19.3, Front-wheel Skids

question: According to the manual, what are the three basic steps to take at any accident?
choice_a: Protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured
choice_b: Call your dispatcher, take photos, exchange insurance information
choice_c: Move the vehicle immediately, block traffic, wait for police
choice_d: Turn off the engine, lock the vehicle, walk away
explanation: The manual lists the basic steps at any accident as: protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.20, Accident Procedures

question: If your vehicle is involved in an accident, what does the manual say you should try to do first to protect the area?
choice_a: Remove all cargo from the vehicle
choice_b: Leave the vehicle exactly where it stopped
choice_c: Disconnect the trailer
choice_d: Get it to the side of the road
explanation: The manual says that if your vehicle is involved in the accident, try to get it to the side of the road to prevent another accident and allow traffic to move.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.20.1, Protect the Area

question: If you do not have a cell phone or CB at an accident scene, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Drive to the nearest police station immediately
choice_b: Assume someone else will call for help
choice_c: Wait until the accident scene has been properly protected, then phone or send someone to phone the police
choice_d: Use the vehicle's horn to signal for help
explanation: The manual instructs that without a cell phone or CB, you should wait until the accident scene has been properly protected, then phone or send someone to phone the police.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.20.2, Notify Authorities

question: What does the manual say about moving a severely injured person at an accident scene?
choice_a: Don't move them unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_b: Only move them if a family member requests it
choice_c: Move them to a comfortable position immediately
choice_d: Always move them away from the vehicle
explanation: The manual says not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.20.3, Care for the Injured

question: How does the manual say to stop heavy bleeding when helping an injured person?
choice_a: Elevate the injured person's legs
choice_b: Apply direct pressure to the wound
choice_c: Apply a tourniquet immediately
choice_d: Pour water on the wound
explanation: The manual instructs stopping heavy bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.20.3, Care for the Injured

question: According to the manual, what can cause a fuel-related vehicle fire?
choice_a: Cold weather and ice on the fuel lines
choice_b: Using diesel instead of gasoline
choice_c: Driver smoking, improper fueling, or loose fuel connections
choice_d: Overinflated tires
explanation: The manual lists driver smoking, improper fueling, and loose fuel connections as causes of vehicle fires related to fuel.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.21.1, Causes of Fire

question: As part of a vehicle inspection for fire prevention, what does the manual say a driver should be sure to check?
choice_a: That the radio antenna is secure
choice_b: That the mud flaps are clean
choice_c: That the spare tire is inflated
choice_d: That the fire extinguisher is charged
explanation: The manual says a complete vehicle inspection for fire prevention should include being sure the fire extinguisher is charged.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.21.2, Fire Prevention

question: If a fire starts in a van or box trailer carrying cargo, what does the manual say to do with the doors?
choice_a: Open them immediately to let smoke escape
choice_b: Keep them shut, especially if the cargo contains hazardous materials
choice_c: Remove them entirely
choice_d: It doesn't matter whether they are open or shut
explanation: The manual instructs keeping the doors shut on a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, especially with hazardous materials, since opening the doors supplies oxygen and can make the fire burn very fast.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.21.3, Fire Fighting (Keep the Fire from Spreading)

question: When using a fire extinguisher, where does the manual say the driver should aim?
choice_a: At the source or base of the fire
choice_b: Up into the flames
choice_c: At the smoke above the fire
choice_d: Anywhere near the vehicle
explanation: The manual instructs aiming the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not up into the flames.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.21.3, Fire Fighting (Extinguish the Fire)

question: Per the manual, which type of fire extinguisher is designed to work on burning wood, paper, and cloth, in addition to electrical fires and burning liquids?
choice_a: The B:C type
choice_b: A plain water extinguisher
choice_c: The D type only
choice_d: The A:B:C type
explanation: The manual states the B:C type extinguisher works on electrical fires and burning liquids, while the A:B:C type is designed to work on burning wood, paper, and cloth as well.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.21.3, Use the Right Fire Extinguisher

question: According to the manual, why should water NOT be used on an electrical fire or a gasoline fire?
choice_a: Water is too expensive to waste
choice_b: Water can cause shock on an electrical fire and will spread the flames on a gasoline fire
choice_c: Water evaporates too slowly to be effective
choice_d: Water damages the fire extinguisher nozzle
explanation: The manual explains water can be used on wood, paper, or cloth, but not on an electrical fire (can cause shock) or a gasoline fire (it will spread the flames).
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.21.3, Use the Right Fire Extinguisher

question: According to the manual, alcohol-related traffic accidents result in how many deaths every year?
choice_a: About 5,000
choice_c: About 500
choice_d: Over 20,000
explanation: The manual states that people who drink alcohol are involved in traffic accidents resulting in over 20,000 deaths every year.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving

question: What does the manual say the liver can process per hour?
choice_a: One-third an ounce of alcohol
choice_b: One full standard drink
choice_c: Two ounces of alcohol
choice_d: Alcohol at whatever rate is consumed
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.1, How Alcohol Works

question: What does the manual say will actually sober a person up after drinking?
choice_a: Black coffee
choice_b: A cold shower
choice_c: Only time
choice_d: Drinking water
explanation: The manual states that because alcohol is processed at a fixed rate, only time, not black coffee or a cold shower, will sober you up.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.1, How Alcohol Works

question: According to the manual's BAC effects chart, a Blood Alcohol Content of .08 represents what?
choice_a: A "mellow feeling" with slight body warmth
choice_b: The point at which most people lose consciousness
choice_c: The drunk driving limit, with impaired coordination and judgment
choice_d: A stage with no noticeable effect
explanation: The manual's BAC effects table lists .08 as showing definite impairment in coordination and judgment, describing it as the drunk driving limit with impaired coordination and judgment.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.1, Effects Of Increasing Blood Alcohol Content

question: According to the manual, which of the following contain the same amount of alcohol?
choice_a: Any two beers, regardless of size
choice_b: A can of soda and a glass of wine
choice_c: Coffee with alcohol added and plain black coffee
choice_d: A 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80 proof liquor
explanation: The manual states that a 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1 1/2-ounce shot of 80 proof liquor all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.1, What Is a Drink?

question: According to the manual, is a driver permitted to use a drug given by a doctor?
choice_a: No, all drugs are prohibited while driving
choice_b: Yes, but only narcotics prescribed for pain
choice_c: Yes, if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability
choice_d: Only if the driver is off duty for 24 hours first
explanation: The manual says possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.2, Other Drugs

question: What does the manual say is the only cure for fatigue?
choice_a: Caffeine
choice_b: A short walk
choice_c: Cold water on the face
choice_d: Rest
explanation: The manual states, "Don't use any drug that hides fatigue--the only cure for fatigue is rest."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.2, Other Drugs

question: If a driver becomes too ill to operate a vehicle safely, what does the manual say about an emergency exception?
choice_a: The driver may drive to the nearest place where they can safely stop
choice_b: The driver may never drive again that day
choice_c: The driver must call a substitute driver before moving the vehicle at all
choice_d: There is no exception; the vehicle must stay parked
explanation: The manual says that if you become too ill to drive safely you must not drive, but in case of an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.22.3, Illness

question: According to the manual, where must a driver keep shipping papers related to hazardous materials while driving?
choice_a: Mailed to the shipper after delivery
choice_b: Stored in the sleeper berth
choice_c: Given to the first responder before starting the trip
choice_d: In a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle
explanation: The manual requires drivers to keep hazardous materials shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.23.2, Why Are There Rules? (To Communicate the Risk)

question: How many identical placards must a placarded hazardous materials vehicle display, and where?
choice_a: Two, on the front and rear only
choice_b: One, on the driver's side only
choice_c: At least four identical placards, on the front, rear, and both sides
choice_d: Three, on both sides and the rear
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, put on the front, rear, and both sides.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.23.3, Lists of Regulated Products

question: What is required before a driver may operate a vehicle that needs placards for hazardous materials?
choice_a: A hazardous materials endorsement on the CDL
choice_b: A valid regular driver's license only
choice_c: A note from the shipper
choice_d: Completion of a defensive driving course
explanation: The manual warns that you cannot drive a vehicle that requires placards unless your driver license has the hazardous materials endorsement; doing so without it is a crime.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 2.23.3, Lists of Regulated Products
